name: HEEYID_VERSION
what: the release to run: the images' tag, the git tag without the `v` (`local`: an image built on this host from heeyid, for a test stand)

name: CONSOLES_ADDRESS
what: the address of the consoles' one door (heeyid-consoles, port 443): the host's address on the network the operators reach it from (the bank's jump host), never 0.0.0.0. It must stay fixed: a static address, or a DHCP reservation; the consoles' names (CONSOLES_DOMAIN) resolve to it

name: CONSOLES_DOMAIN
what: the domain the consoles are named under: vault., keycloak., grafana. and mailpit. + it, each through the door on CONSOLES_ADDRESS, each certificate naming its name. The platform maps the names to CONSOLES_ADDRESS: the bank's DNS (one record, *.<domain>), or /etc/hosts on a lone machine

name: CALLBACKS_ADDRESS
what: the address of the door for the SMS vendors' delivery reports (heeyid-callbacks, port 8080, plain HTTP): the host's address on the network the bank's ingress reaches it from, never 0.0.0.0. The ingress ends TLS for the public URL and passes only `/delivery-reports/` here; it must stay fixed

name: LOG_MAX_SIZE
what: a container's log file size before Docker rotates it (`k` or `m`); the collector ships each line as it is written, so rotation loses nothing

name: LOG_MAX_FILES
what: how many rotated log files Docker keeps per container

name: VAULT_AUDIT_MAX_MB
what: the size in MB at which Vault's audit file is rotated (Vault reopens it, no line lost)

name: VAULT_AUDIT_KEEP
what: how many rotated audit files stay on Vault's volume; the bank's SIEM keeps the year

name: MAILPIT
what: `on` runs the mail catcher for heeyID's alerts (`mailpit:1025`, inbox https://mailpit.<CONSOLES_DOMAIN>); `off` runs none (its image is never pulled)

name: PULL_ATTEMPTS
what: how many times `up` and `deploy` try to pull the images before giving up

name: PULL_RETRY_SECONDS
what: the seconds between two pull tries

name: GF_SMTP_HOST
what: Grafana's mail relay, `host:port`

name: GF_SMTP_USER
what: the relay's login; empty without one

name: GF_SMTP_PASSWORD
what: the relay's password; empty without one

name: GF_SMTP_STARTTLS_POLICY
what: `NoStartTLS` with Mailpit, `MandatoryStartTLS` with a real relay

name: GF_SMTP_FROM_ADDRESS
what: the alerts' sender: an address whose domain has a dot (Grafana refuses one without)

name: ALERT_EMAILS
what: where alerts go, `;`-separated

name: MYID_BASE_URL
what: MyID's host for this zone (`{myid_host}` in MyID's documentation): its test environment on stage, its production service in production (SAD §6, zone separation). `https://<host>`, no path

name: MYID_MEDIA_URL
what: MyID's media host for this zone (`{myid_media_host}`, the Inplace photo upload), from the same contract as MYID_BASE_URL

name: MYID_TRUSTED_CAS
what: the CA that signed MyID's certificates for this zone (PEM; the installer asks for the file). The adapter trusts MyID only through it (SAD TB-5, pinned CA)

name: MYID_CLIENT_ID
what: heeyID's MyID client_id, from the bank's contract with MyID for this zone (one per installation, SAD C-13)

name: MYID_CLIENT_SECRET
what: that client's client_secret

name: MYID_USERNAME
what: the MyID login for the Backend API without personal data (photo comparison, the password grant), from the same contract

name: MYID_PASSWORD
what: that login's password

name: XABAR_USERNAME
what: heeyID's login at SMS Xabar (Play Mobile SMS-Broker API, Basic auth), from the bank's contract with Xabar

name: XABAR_PASSWORD
what: that login's password

name: XABAR_ORIGINATOR
what: the sender name the bank registered at Xabar: what the customer sees as the sender

name: XABAR_ADDRESSES
what: the addresses Xabar sends its delivery reports from (ask Xabar): IPv4 addresses or networks, comma separated. heeyid-callbacks takes a report only for one of them, as the bank's ingress names it in X-Forwarded-For

name: CALLBACKS_INGRESS_ADDRESSES
what: the addresses the bank's ingress connects to CALLBACKS_ADDRESS from: IPv4 addresses or networks, comma separated. heeyid-callbacks takes no connection from anywhere else, and trusts X-Forwarded-For only from these

name: TAF_AUTH_URL
what: TAF's (Telecom AntiFraud) OAuth 2.0 token endpoint for this zone, the full URL, from the bank's contract with TAF

name: TAF_AGENT_URL
what: the TAF agent in the bank's network (its API host) for this zone: `https://<host>[:<port>]`

name: TAF_HEALTH_URL
what: the TAF agent's health, the full URL (the agent's host, port 8081, `/actuator/health`)

name: TAF_TRUSTED_CAS
what: the CA that signed TAF's certificates for this zone (PEM; the installer asks for the file). The adapter trusts TAF only through it (SAD TB-5, pinned CA)

name: TAF_CLIENT_ID
what: heeyID's TAF client_id (client_credentials), from the bank's contract with TAF for this zone, one per installation

name: TAF_CLIENT_SECRET
what: that client's client_secret

name: TAF_SCOPE
what: the scope TAF gives that client (the token request's `scope`), from the same contract

name: FCM_PROJECT_ID
what: the bank's Firebase project for this zone (its project ID, as Firebase's console shows it): the push adapter sends through it only

name: FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT
what: the JSON key of that project's service account with role `roles/firebasecloudmessaging.admin` (the installer asks for the file; docs/install-server.md, "The FCM credential"). Only the push adapter gets it, as a file

name: LDAP_URL
what: the bank's directory (Active Directory or another LDAP server) the consoles' people sign in with, over TLS only: `ldaps://<host>[:<port>]`. Keycloak reads people and their two groups from it, never writes; their passwords stay there

name: LDAP_TRUSTED_CAS
what: the CA that signed the directory's certificate (PEM; the installer asks for the file)

name: LDAP_VENDOR
what: `ad` for Active Directory, `other` for another LDAP server (OpenLDAP, 389 Directory Server, …)

name: LDAP_BIND_DN
what: the directory account Keycloak reads with: read-only on the people and the two groups, nothing else

name: LDAP_BIND_PASSWORD
what: that account's password

name: LDAP_USERS_DN
what: where the people are, searched with everything below it

name: LDAP_USER_OBJECT_CLASSES
what: the object classes of a person, comma-separated: `person, organizationalPerson, user` in Active Directory, `inetOrgPerson, organizationalPerson` in OpenLDAP

name: LDAP_USERNAME_ATTRIBUTE
what: the attribute people sign in with: `sAMAccountName` in Active Directory, `uid` in OpenLDAP

name: LDAP_UUID_ATTRIBUTE
what: the attribute that names a person for ever, even renamed: `objectGUID` in Active Directory, `entryUUID` in OpenLDAP

name: LDAP_ADMINS_GROUP_DN
what: the directory group of the consoles' admins: Grafana's Admin role and Keycloak's admin console. Its direct members count (not those of a group nested in it); a DN with an escaped character (`\`) isn't taken; the directory must give people the `memberOf` attribute (Active Directory always does; OpenLDAP with its memberof overlay)

name: LDAP_VIEWERS_GROUP_DN
what: the directory group of the consoles' viewers: Grafana's Viewer role. Someone in neither group can't sign in to any console; removed from a group in the directory, they lose it at their next sign-in

name: CONSOLE_LOCKOUT_FAILURES
what: failed sign-ins in a row before an account is locked, 10 at most

name: CONSOLE_LOCKOUT_MINUTES
what: how long a locked account stays locked, 30 minutes or more

name: CONSOLE_IDLE_MINUTES
what: idle minutes before a console session ends, 15 at most

name: KEYCLOAK_KEY_ROTATE_DAYS
what: the token signing keys' cryptoperiod in days, 365 at most: keycloak-config makes a new key this often in every realm and retires the old one a period later

name: LOG_SHIP_PROTOCOL
what: how every log line also goes to the bank's observability, when the bank gives a collector: `otlp` (OTLP/HTTP over TLS) or `syslog` (RFC 5424 over TCP with TLS); `off` keeps them in this stack only (they always stay here too)

name: LOG_SHIP_ENDPOINT
what: the bank's log collector: `https://<host>:<port>/<path>` (the full OTLP logs URL) for otlp, `<host>:<port>` for syslog; observability checks it answers when it starts. Empty with `off`

name: METRICS_SHIP_ENDPOINT
what: the bank's OTLP/HTTP metrics URL, `https://<host>:<port>/<path>` in full (e.g. …/v1/metrics), when the bank gives one; observability checks it answers when it starts. Empty: the metrics stay in this stack only

name: TRACES_SHIP_ENDPOINT
what: the bank's OTLP/HTTP traces URL, `https://<host>:<port>/<path>` in full (e.g. …/v1/traces), when the bank gives one. Empty: the traces stay in this stack only

name: SHIP_TRUSTED_CAS
what: the CA that signed the bank's collectors' certificates (PEM; the installer asks for the file). Empty when nothing is shipped

name: SHIP_AUTHORIZATION
what: the `Authorization` header the bank's OTLP collectors want, as it is sent (e.g. `Bearer <token>` or `Basic <base64>`); not sent to syslog. Empty when they want none

name: CERT_ALERT_DAYS
what: days before a certificate's end that Grafana alerts, daily until it is renewed: the services', the consoles', the CAs, the callers' client certificates. Below 30: `apply` renews heeyID's own certificates in their last 30 days, so a longer lead would alert on ones it hasn't renewed yet
